text: {"memo": "As of March 31, 2025, Pfizer’s most recently completed fiscal year was 2024. In FY2024, the company reported revenue of $63.6 billion, up about 9% from $58.5 billion in FY2023, as COVID product revenue normalized and non-COVID sales grew. GAAP net income was about $8.2 billion, and diluted EPS was roughly $2.96 for the full year, according to the company’s adjusted reporting. Operating cash flow was strong at around $10.9 billion. The fiscal year 2024 net margin was modest, around 13%, with operating margin near 25%. In FY2023, revenue fell sharply to $58.5 billion from $100.3 billion in FY2022, a decline of about 41%, because of reduced COVID vaccine and treatment demand. GAAP net income was about $9.1 billion, and diluted EPS was near $2.0. Margins compressed. FY2022 had revenue of $100.3 billion, net income of $31.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.29, driven by COVID-related sales. The 2024 rebound is encouraging but not a full recovery. The stock as of 2025-03-31 would be viewed cautiously, with confidence restored only if pipeline catalysts and margin improvement continue. One-line view: PFE is a cash-rich, dividend-paying pharma name facing a transitional growth year, but the stock is a hold for long-term investors awaiting new oncology and vaccine launches."}
